questions.q: In a Contract Account, **retention money** represents the portion of the
options: Value of work certified that is temporarily withheld by the contractee as security against potential defects during the maintenance period
Architect's professional fees paid in advance before construction commences on site
Value of uncertified work retained by the contractor at the end of the year
Initial tender deposit forfeited to the client in the event of contractual default
questions.explain: **Retention money** is a percentage (often $10\%$ to $20\%$) of the architect-certified progress payment that the contractee (client) holds back from the contractor. It serves as a safeguard to ensure the contractor remedies any faulty workmanship or defects that appear during the agreed defects liability period.

questions.q:
Use the following details extracted from a contractor's ledger to determine the **Notional Profit** on a contract:

*   Value of work certified: ₦120,000
*   Cost of work uncertified: ₦15,000
*   Total cost of contract to date: ₦95,000
questions.explain:
**Notional Profit** is calculated as the total value of work done to date minus the total contract costs incurred to date:

$$\text{Total Value of Work Done} = \text{Value of Work Certified} + \text{Cost of Work Uncertified}$$
$$\text{Total Value of Work Done} = ₦120,000 + ₦15,000 = ₦135,000$$

$$\text{Notional Profit} = ₦135,000 - \text{Total Cost to Date} (₦95,000) = ₦40,000$$
